title: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Solomon Islands: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Solomon Islands: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step serious and terminal illness checklist for Solomon Islands: palliative care coordination, advance directives, powers of attorney, disability and caregiver support, and estate preparation.
introHtml: Preparing medical, workplace, superannuation, civil registration, and estate paperwork in advance in Solomon Islands reduces urgent uncertainty for families navigating Honiara and provincial offices. Aligning Wills, beneficiary nominations, identity documents, and tax filings under domestic statutes helps ensure institutions can act promptly without avoidable court or administrative delays [2][7][12].

steps.title: Healthcare coordination and statutory workplace leave
steps.html:
• Coordinate clinical care, specialist referrals, and medical-incapacity documentation through the Ministry of Health and Medical Services and National Referral Hospital (NRH) in Honiara (+677 44000 switchboard; +677 23600 general line; +677 21068 Emergency Operations Centre) or regional provincial hospitals [6][14].
  • Review workplace paid sick leave, notice periods, and medical-ground cessation protections under the Labour Act (Chapter 73) and the Employment Act (Chapter 72) (labour.gov.sb), as formal cessation of employment on certified medical grounds frequently intersects with early superannuation withdrawal eligibility [7][10][11].
  • Discuss treatment preferences openly with the attending medical team and close family members while the patient has clear legal capacity, keeping current clinical records organized [6][14].

steps.title: Drafting a compliant Will, customary land limits, and proxy readiness
steps.html:
• Execute or update a formal written Will complying with the Wills, Probate and Administration Act 1987 (parliament.gov.sb): the maker must be aged 18 or older (s. 4), sign in writing in the simultaneous presence of two witnesses (s. 5(1)(a)), and note that a subsequent marriage automatically revokes a prior Will unless statutory exceptions apply (s. 10(2)) [2].
  • Keep separate records for customary land and personal property, because Section 2(3) and Section 2(4) expressly exclude customary land and customary usage from the Act's testamentary operation [2].
  • Inform the named executor or trusted family member where the original signed Will is held, noting that under Section 107 any person holding a Will faces a statutory duty to deposit it with the High Court or local Magistrate within 30 days once probate events arise; verify any Registrar General's Office (+677 23002) questions early and arrange financial Powers of Attorney with legal counsel if banking assistance is needed during care [2][5].

steps.title: Solomon Islands National Provident Fund (SINPF) incapacity & nominations
steps.html:
• Audit active member details and verify filed beneficiary nominations with Solomon Islands National Provident Fund (SINPF) (+677 21852; enquiry@sinpf.org.sb), reviewing the Resources forms library and Unclaimed Deposits register [4][7][8][9].
  • Under SINPF rules, members certified physically or mentally incapacitated by qualified medical authorities and unable to continue regular employment qualify for a full lump-sum Medical Incapacity withdrawal (with certain early-release exemptions gazetted under statutory Ministerial/Board authority) [7].
  • Keep beneficiary birth or marriage certificates verified alongside valid government IDs so members remain eligible for the SBD 10,000 Special Death Benefit (SDB) and smooth account payout without unclaimed-deposit freezes [7][8].

steps.title: Vital record accuracy, tax status, and safe custody
steps.html:
• Confirm matching names, dates of birth, and relationship particulars across birth and marriage certificates governed by the Births and Deaths (Registration) Act 1988 and Ministry of Home Affairs vital records before filing institutional claims [1][3].
  • Verify personal income tax, PAYE, or business compliance with Inland Revenue Division (IRD) at the Ministry of Finance Building, Mendana Ave, Honiara (+677 21493 Honiara Office; +677 28307 Income Tax; Monday to Friday 8:00 AM to 4:30 PM) [12][13]. Solomon Islands does not levy a separate inheritance or estate tax [12][13].
  • Store original signed Wills, SINPF statements, land leases, insurance policies, and bank details in a known secure place [2][7].

steps.title: Cross-border legalisation readiness and household inventory
steps.html:
• If family members, pensions, or bank accounts are outside Solomon Islands, note that Solomon Islands is not a Contracting Party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention [15]. Certified vital certificates and High Court grants used overseas therefore require diplomatic or consular legalisation rather than a Hague Apostille [15].
  • Build a clear written dossier covering SINPF member number, IRD taxpayer details, domestic and foreign bank accounts, employer HR contacts, Registrar General's Office references, and Will location [2][5][7][12].
  • Verify overseas bank signatory rules early if international medical travel or cross-border support could occur [14][15].

contacts.name: Registrar General's Office
contacts.note: Hibiscus Avenue, Point Cruz, Honiara; coordinates civil registry and Public Trustee/estate filings under Ministry of Justice and Legal Affairs.

contacts.note: Ministry of Finance Building, Mendana Ave, Honiara (P.O. Box G9); Income Tax line +677 28307, Mon-Fri 8:00 AM-4:30 PM.
